components.risk: Moderate: HTTP/2 and HPACK process remote-controlled headers; unchecked UTF-8 relies on the BytesStr constructor invariant.
components.boundary: src/hpack/header.rs:276-283 validates Bytes with str::from_utf8 before storing them in a private tuple field, then uses from_utf8_unchecked when exposing a string. The other constructors consume str or static str. No foreign-function boundary was found in the source unsafe-token search.
components.justification: Name::into_entry uses BytesStr::try_from for authority, scheme and path, while ordinary header fields use HeaderValue::from_bytes. BytesStr owns immutable Bytes and exposes no mutable byte reference in the inspected implementation; these facts support the checked-on-construction UTF-8 invariant. Retention supplies HTTP/2 for the selected Hyper client/server graph; deleting it would remove an active protocol capability, not just an optional accelerator. The crate denies missing safety documentation but does not forbid unsafe.
components.residual_risk: This is not a complete HPACK/state-machine or denial-of-service audit. It does not prove every future constructor preserves UTF-8, nor verify every HTTP/2 limit or concurrency interleaving. Exact-source advisory and end-to-end network tests remain required.

components.risk: High: network-facing HTTP parsing and read-buffer initialization combine unchecked header conversion, MaybeUninit and pin/lifetime operations.
components.boundary: src/rt/io.rs tracks raw capacity, initialized bytes and filled bytes; the initialized-slice view and cursor lifetime narrowing are unsafe. HTTP/1 role.rs reads only parser-reported initialized header slots and constructs HeaderValue without rechecking validated bytes. These selected Rust internals differ from the unselected ffi/capi interface.
components.justification: ReadBuf::new records the full initialized input length; filled() restricts the exposed slice to the filled prefix. The cursor is borrowed from a stable underlying buffer and narrows its lifetime. The server parser returns on partial/error parses, records initialized header indices after successful httparse parsing, then iterates only headers_len. These inspected invariants explain the unsafe optimization boundary without erasing it from inventory. Retention provides the selected HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 client/server engine required by Susi networking and MCP transports.
components.residual_risk: Custom unsafe cursor users must not deinitialize bytes or advance past initialized data. Header validity depends on httparse and all unchecked-conversion call sites. The HTTP parser, cancellation and protocol-smuggling cases were not exhaustively audited or fuzzed here; large body/header budgets remain a product-level concern.

components.risk: High: async I/O adaptation and synchronization make unsafe initialization and Sync contracts observable through safe network APIs.
components.boundary: TokioIo polls AsyncRead into the Hyper cursor as a Tokio uninitialized buffer, then advances by exactly tbuf.filled().len(). SyncWrapper<T> implements Sync for T:Send while exposing the value only through exclusive access or ownership. The inspected if_nametoindex FFI is cfg-gated to Apple/Solaris-like platforms, not Linux.
components.justification: The adapter returns early for Pending/error and advances only after a successful read. SyncWrapper has no shared-reference accessor for its inner value, supporting its declared exclusive-access rationale. Linux interface binding calls socket.bind_device rather than the inspected if_nametoindex block. Retention supplies Tokio compatibility, connection pooling and client/server utilities for the selected HTTP stack; these are active capabilities. The local facade forbids new unsafe in Susi wrapper code without pretending that this forbids upstream internals.
components.residual_risk: The adapter inherits the safety contract of the underlying AsyncRead implementation. Proxy policy, DNS, socket and cancellation behavior were not exhaustively checked. Apple system proxy unsafe calls are outside this Linux review and require their own platform qualification.

components.justification: These inspected representation, UTF-8 and allocation invariants support the specific unsafe optimizations. components.risk: High adapter boundary: lifetime/pin projection, reusable futures and libc byte search depend on unchecked invariants in safe stream/channel APIs.
components.boundary: Selected io exports manually pin-project StreamReader.inner, with Unpin conditional on S. write_all_vectored extends only a shared sub-IoSlice lifetime back to its original backing buffer lifetime. PollSender erases a future lifetime but stores it within a T-parameterized owner. Selected Unix libc memchr bounds the call by the input slice and checks null before pointer-offset conversion.
components.justification: The inspected projection pins only inner and exposes other fields unpinned. IoSlice advancement uses checked subtraction to avoid cumulative-length overflow, retaining the original shared backing data. PollSender documents that its future never escapes its T-bearing owner. These utilities support selected streaming bodies and codec transports in HTTP/MCP and Docker. Retention keeps these required adaptations while recording actual upstream unsafe boundaries.

components.risk: High type-erasure boundary: raw pointer/inline storage, destructor callbacks and erased lifetimes can violate memory safety if type/lifetime contracts diverge.
components.boundary: Any stores values inline only when both size and alignment fit, otherwise in a Box converted to a raw pointer. It retains a matching drop callback and typeid::of<T>. take checks the type ID, transfers the value, and forgets the original container to avoid double destruction. Any::new is unsafe because borrowed T must not outlive its referent.
components.justification: The inspected Any implementation explicitly records and enforces representation/type invariants and restores Box ownership for heap values. de::Out wraps creation/take for erased deserializer results; unsafe-map helpers propagate these operations only for successful values. Retention provides selected typetag trait-object serialization through Tantivy in the document index, with alloc enabled and std/unstable-debug absent.
components.residual_risk: A type ID check cannot prove erased borrow lifetimes, and correctness depends on every call site pairing the right T and limiting lifetime. All serializer/deserializer vtable paths were not exhaustively audited. Exact-version pinning, index tests and upstream advisory checks remain required.
